questions.question: What is a productive first step when a group receives a complex task?
choices: Clarify the goal, constraints, and roles
Begin separate work without discussing the goal
Choose a final answer before reading the task
Assign every role to one person

questions.question: A team member has not spoken. What can another member do to support collaboration?
choices: Assume the member has no ideas
Invite the member to share their perspective without putting them on the spot
Speak for the member
End the conversation

questions.question: Two group members disagree about a solution. What should they compare?
choices: Who has the louder voice
Which proposal was mentioned first
The evidence and criteria relevant to each proposal
Which member is more popular

questions.question: Why should a group summarize decisions before ending a meeting?
choices: To prevent members from asking questions
To avoid recording responsibilities
To make the meeting longer
To confirm shared understanding and clarify next steps

questions.question: A group assigns one person to research, one to check evidence, and one to report. What is the benefit?
choices: Responsibilities are clear and work can be coordinated
No one needs to communicate
The task is guaranteed to be correct
Members cannot contribute outside their role

questions.question: Which response best handles a misunderstanding?
choices: Assume the worst intention
Ask the speaker to clarify and restate what you understood
Repeat the misunderstood idea as fact
Stop listening

questions.question: A team is behind schedule. Which action is most constructive?
choices: Blame one person before checking progress
Ignore the deadline
Identify the remaining tasks, set priorities, and redistribute work fairly
Discard the shared goal

questions.question: What does building on a peer's idea involve?
choices: Repeat the idea and claim it as your own
Reject it without explanation
Change to an unrelated topic
Acknowledge the idea and add a related point or question

questions.question: Which group norm helps make disagreement productive?
choices: Challenge ideas with reasons while treating members respectfully
Never question a proposal
Criticize the person who proposed it
Let only the leader speak

questions.question: A group agrees quickly, but one member has concerns. What should the facilitator do?
choices: Declare the decision final
Invite the concern and check whether the decision addresses it
Exclude the member from later work
Pretend agreement is complete

questions.question: A group uses a shared document. Which practice improves accountability?
choices: Delete names from all tasks
Let everyone assume someone else will do it
Record owners and due dates for each task
Avoid reviewing progress

questions.question: What is consensus?
choices: A decision made by the fastest speaker
A rule that everyone must share the same opinion
A vote that ignores discussion
A decision the group can support after considering perspectives, even if it is not everyone's first choice

questions.question: A member interrupts repeatedly. Which reminder is most useful?
choices: Let's finish each turn and make sure everyone has a chance to contribute
Stop talking forever
Your ideas are not useful
Only the leader may speak

questions.question: Why can assigning a rotating facilitator help a group?
choices: It removes the need for group decisions
It shares responsibility for keeping discussion focused and equitable
It makes one member responsible for all content
It prevents disagreement

questions.question: A group receives feedback that its presentation lacks evidence. What is the best response?
choices: Dismiss all feedback as unfair
Add unrelated quotations
Review the claim and add relevant, credible support
Remove the claim without discussion

questions.question: Which statement demonstrates paraphrasing in conversation?
choices: I disagree
Whatever
Let's move on
So your concern is that the schedule leaves too little time for testing—is that right?

questions.question: A group is choosing among options with different costs and benefits. What should it do?
choices: Agree on criteria, compare options, and explain the trade-offs
Choose at random
Compare each option using different criteria
Ignore affected stakeholders

questions.question: How can a recorder support a collaborative group?
choices: Decide the answer without consulting others
Capture decisions, questions, and assigned next steps
Record only personal opinions
Prevent members from revising ideas

questions.question: A member misses a meeting. How can the group support continuity?
choices: Restart all work without explanation
Assume the member will guess what happened
Share the decisions and assigned tasks with that member
Remove the member's responsibilities without notice

questions.question: Which reflection best evaluates collaboration?
choices: Rate the group by who spoke most
Focus only on whether the task was finished
List members' personalities
Consider how listening, role-sharing, and evidence influenced the group's result
